messages:
Maya: Heads-up — we need a new GPU nodepool for a low-latency embeddings endpoint in us-central3. Goal: steady 2k rps, p99 < 120ms for small requests. Looking for cost/sku tradeoffs and autoscaler settings.

Sanjay: what are the workload shapes? short seq len or batches?

Maya: mostly short sequences (<128 tokens), many parallel small requests. Occasional batched offline jobs. Prefer 1 GPU per pod if possible to avoid noisy neighbors.

Leo: For that profile I'd mix L4/T4-like skus for cheap inference and a small A100 pool for batched fallback. But packing matters — 1 GPU per pod is wasteful on A100, better to pin multiple pods per GPU for batching.

Ashley: FYI quota check: current project has A100 GPU quota 4 in us-central3, T4 quota 40. Need a quota request if we want >4 A100s. Also network egress IPs limited in that region.

Maya: ok let's design two pools: "lowlat-embed-t4" (cheap, scale to 30) and "batch-a100" (small, scale 0-6). Taints to avoid accidental scheduling?

Leo: yes — use taints and nodeAffinity. Proposed taints:

```
node.kubernetes.io/gpu: "true":NoSchedule
pool.role: "batch":NoSchedule
```

And for the cheap pool: `pool.role: lowlat:PreferNoSchedule` (so can spill).

Sanjay: cluster-autoscaler flags we should adjust: --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m (shorter), --balance-similar-node-groups=false so mixed skus can co-exist, and set expander=least-waste.

Maya: can you paste an example gcloud create command we can use?

Sanjay: sure — for the T4 pool:

```
gcloud container node-pools create lowlat-embed-t4 \
  --cluster=prod-cluster \
  --zone=us-central3-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-16 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-t4,count=1 \
  --num-nodes=3 \
  --min-nodes=1 --max-nodes=30 \
  --node-labels=pool=lowlat,gpu=true \
  --node-taints=pool.role=lowlat:PreferNoSchedule,gpu=true:NoSchedule \
  --enable-autoscaling
```

And for the A100 batch pool:

```
gcloud container node-pools create batch-a100 \
  --cluster=prod-cluster \
  --zone=us-central3-a \
  --machine-type=n2-highmem-32 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-a100,count=1 \
  --num-nodes=0 \
  --min-nodes=0 --max-nodes=6 \
  --node-labels=pool=batch,gpu=true \
  --node-taints=pool.role=batch:NoSchedule,gpu=true:NoSchedule \
  --enable-autoscaling
```

Ashley: Also add podPriorityClass for embed requests so the autoscaler doesn't evict them during scale-down. And set scale-down-delay-after-add=5m to avoid thrash during bursts.

Maya: What about scheduling small pods onto shared GPUs? We said 1 GPU per pod earlier but maybe use fractional packing for T4. Any runtime config?

Leo: For T4 we can use device-plugin + NVIDIA MPS/GPUslice in the runtime to host multiple containers per GPU. But it requires kubelet flags + driver setup. If we can't enable that quickly, set requests.limits.gpu=1 for A100 and 0.25 or use CPU-backed for very small ones on CPU nodes.

Sanjay: Cost note: A100 heavy pool at max 6 nodes ~= $X/hr — we should enable preemptible for batch-a100 nodes to cut costs, but mark batch jobs as fault-tolerant.

Maya: I'll open a quota increase ticket with GCP for A100 to request +12 GPUs in us-central3. Ashley can you own that?

Ashley: on it — filing now. ETA for approval usually 24-72h. Linking request: https://console.cloud.google.com/quotas?id=proj:REDACTED

infra-bot: Deployment check: kube-ops-runner shows node image family mismatch on N2 vs N1. Ensure node image has NVIDIA drivers preinstalled.

Sanjay: Good catch. Add --image-type=UBUNTU_CONTAINERD and post-install script to install drivers. Also add toleration for gpu operator daemonset.

Maya: Action items: (1) Ashley files quota increase, (2) S to prepare gcloud + node pool templates and autoscaler flags PR, (3) Leo to document runtime GPU packing options and cost tradeoffs, (4) I'll schedule a ten-minute rollout window for the pools tomorrow 09:30 PT.

devops-bot: Reminder scheduled: 2024-10-22T16:30:00Z - create-gpu-nodepools (assigned: Maya)

Ashley: Quota ticket submitted — number QT-2024-1123. Keeping thread updated when approved. :white_check_mark:

Maya: thanks all — we'll iterate after first traffic test. If quotas are slow, we can start with T4-only and use batch fallback to off-cluster GPUs.
